entry.evidence: A local data assimilation method, Local DA, is designed to fulfill these needs.

sequences.source_document: Publisher XML text (jats_text) of the published paper, with PDF for figures

steps.action: The authors take from the literature the expectations that hybrid covariance helps with small ensembles and that multiscale localization beats fixed localization.
steps.quote: Recent studies have shown that multiscale DA outperforms DA with fixed localization

steps.action: The authors propose a flexible local scheme that keeps the LETKF's grid-independent analysis but allows hybrid and multiscale analysis without a large static ensemble.
steps.quote: it is desirable to design a flexible DA scheme that follows the grid-independent analysis of the LETKF

steps.action: The authors pose four questions: how to do local hybrid and multiscale analysis, spatial continuity, impact of hybrid covariance and multiscale localization, and cycling performance; they also scope the LETKF comparison.
steps.quote: this study focuses on the following main issues: (i) how to locally conduct the hybrid and multiscale analysis

steps.action: The authors formulate Local DA: a cost function over an explicit local correlation matrix Coo rescaled by alpha, a CG solver with a 100-iteration cap, stochastic ensemble update, and the Tang et al. (2014) observation-operator approximation.
steps.quote: Local DA adopts an iterative algorithm, namely, the conjugate gradient (CG) method (Shewchuk, 1994)

steps.action: In early tests (not shown) the authors check that the localized error-sample matrix is near full rank, and that the chosen observation-operator approximation lowers reflectivity error by about 2 dBZ compared with the ensemble mean of priors.
steps.quote: Our early test (not shown) indicates that X ^ o is a full rank matrix in most cases.

steps.action: The authors add model-space multiscale localization (bandpass decomposition, per-scale radius, no cross-scale covariance), observation-space and double-space localization, a hybrid static-plus-ensemble correlation, the workflow, and N-column analysis.
steps.quote: We perform localization for each scale independently to construct the multiscale correlation matrix.

steps.action: The authors check (not shown) that the five-column analysis only slightly raises errors relative to the one-column analysis while cutting wall-clock time to about 1/N.
steps.quote: the N -column analysis is slightly rasterized (not shown), leading to slightly higher errors than the one-column analysis

steps.action: The authors design a perfect-model OSSE: a WRF 5 km truth simulation of Typhoon In-fa (2021) started from GFS analysis.
steps.quote: The third typhoon of the 2021 western Pacific season, In-fa, is selected for the OSSEs performed herein.

steps.action: The authors check the nature run against CMA best-track central pressure and position (not shown), following the Hoffman and Atlas criterion.
steps.quote: a criterion for reasonable OSSEs is that true simulation agrees with the real atmosphere

steps.action: The authors build a simulated multiscale network (soundings, wind profilers, PWV, three radars), a 15-member time-lagged ensemble, 14 single-analysis configurations, and three cycling experiments.
steps.quote: A total of 14 experiments for deterministic analyses at 00:00 UTC on 26 July 2021 are examined.

steps.action: The authors report, without showing it, that a 36-member ensemble gives lower analysis errors than the 15-member ensemble.
steps.quote: The authors have tested a larger ensemble with 36 members and obtained lower analysis errors than the 15-member counterpart.

steps.action: The authors map CG iteration counts and cost-function reduction across the domain; convergence is slow where observations are dense, but no severe discontinuity appears.
steps.quote: The results also indicate that no severe discontinuity occurs in Hybrid_5band, which is desired.

steps.action: After finding that about 25 % of minimizations fail to converge in 100 steps, the authors rerun with radar data only and with a 500-iteration cap, and trace the slow convergence to radar data.
steps.quote: we rerun Hybrid_5band using only radar data and observe that only 4 % of all minimizations require more than 100 steps to converge

steps.action: The authors compare domain-averaged RMSEs in observation and model space for all configurations against the truth and against the background (BAK).
steps.quote: All experiments reduce the errors in the observation space after DA, but their differences are significant (Table 4).

steps.action: The authors check (not shown) that errors restricted to the convective area behave like the small-scale versus large-scale errors, so the scale decomposition is used instead.
steps.quote: The difference between errors in the convective area (reflectivity > 10 dBZ) and the rest of the area is similar

steps.action: The authors compare scale-decomposed errors for the hybrid, multiscale and double-space configurations; restricting small-scale correlation reduces small-scale error, though qv error rises with more bands.
steps.quote: This result confirms the assumption that restricting the impact of small-scale correlation in a small region is beneficial.

steps.action: The authors use a second error metric, the difference in total energy, at three levels; it shows hybrid multiscale and double-space localization suppress spurious increments.
steps.quote: To qualitatively assess the analysis error, we compute the difference in total energy (DTE; Meng and Zhang, 2007).

steps.action: The authors compare Local DA with observation-space localization against an LETKF run with the same horizontal localization; errors and increments are similar.
steps.quote: Overall, in the case of using observation-space localization, Local DA can produce an analysis similar to the LETKF.

steps.action: The authors diagnose the ensemble's scale-dependent spread-to-error relation and use it to explain the qv mismatch, attributing it to the ensemble rather than to the localization idea.
steps.quote: it is not irrational for Ens_5band and Hybrid_5band to produce a higher analysis error for q v than Ens_2band

steps.action: In 6 h cycling, the authors compare surface-pressure tendency (an imbalance metric) against the truth for the hybrid multiscale double-space and ensemble-only configurations.
steps.quote: By 18:00 UTC, Hybrid_5band_DSL_6h reaches the balance status, while Ens_noFLTR_6h does not.

steps.action: The authors shorten the cycling interval to 3 h and find that imbalance is not suppressed and errors oscillate, which limits the advantage to sufficiently long intervals.
steps.quote: When the cycling interval becomes shorter (Hybrid_5band_DSL_3h), the ps tendency cannot be effectively suppressed as Hybrid_5band_DSL_6h does.

steps.action: The authors compare cycling forecast and analysis RMSE evolution, final-time error maps, and the evolution of spread versus RMSE between the configurations.
steps.quote: The above result confirms the benefit of using the hybrid covariance and multiscale localization.

steps.action: The authors characterize computational performance: OpenMP scaling up to 16 cores, 225 s run time, the share of cost by step, and about 4 GB of memory against the LETKF's hundreds of MB.
steps.quote: the wall clock time is reduced by approximately 50 % upon doubling the number of cores

steps.action: The authors retain five conclusions: no severe CG discontinuity, affordable Coo with thinning, a hybrid benefit, a multiscale benefit at small scale with further gain from double-space localization, and acceptable efficiency.
steps.quote: Local DA can effectively utilize the hybrid covariance to produce a better analysis than the analysis using ensemble covariance with a fixed localization radius.

steps.action: The authors restrict the double-space recommendation to noisy covariances and 3-D DA, and list refinements: an MPI-OpenMP scheme, an objective static covariance, better multiscale localization, cross-variable balance, and parameter sensitivity.
steps.quote: whether to use double-space localization should be considered case by case

sequences.source_document: Open discussion record of gmd-2022-112 (RC1, RC2 with supplement, AC1 with supplement)

steps.action: Referee 1 asked for formula-level details of the multiscale localization; the authors added Eqs. (15)–(16) and the example table (Table 2).
steps.quote: Details on the realization of the multiscale localization analysis are added.

steps.action: Referee 1 questioned identical static correlation lengths for all variables; the authors explained the per-variable radii (200, 1000, 20 km) and deferred improvement, with no new experiments.
steps.quote: The influence radii of the static correlation are independently set for each analysis variable

steps.action: Referee 1 asked why the static cross-variable term is zeroed; the authors explained that unobserved variables are updated only through the ensemble cross-correlation, adding text but no new work.
steps.quote: The current Local DA updates the unobserved model variables via the cross-variable correlation computed using the ensemble covariance.

steps.action: Referee 1 asked for the nature run to be checked against the real atmosphere (Hoffman and Atlas 2016); the authors compared it with CMA central pressure and position.
steps.quote: We compared the typhoon central-pressure (ps) at sea level of the Truth simulation and the observations published by the China Meteorological Administration (CMA).

steps.action: Referee 1 asked about the sensitivity to localization lengths and wavebands; the authors redesigned the experiments (2-, 3- and 5-band, Static_BE), renamed them, and removed LDA_DS_noENS and the 36-member results.
steps.quote: we add new experiments to test multiscale localization parameters

steps.action: Referee 1's minor comments led the authors to correct the Cmo example and add Figure 2, which shows the bandpass-decomposed perturbations and the spread contribution by scale.
steps.quote: We added a new figure (Figure 2) and the related text for a decomposed member.

steps.action: Referee 1 supplied an auxiliary explanation for slow CG convergence (small hydrometeor mixing ratios in reflectivity assimilation); the authors adopted it in the text.
steps.quote: The inefficient minimization may be caused by the assimilation of radar reflectivity due to the use of the mixing ratios as state variables.

steps.action: Referee 1 asked for elaboration of the LETKF comparison; the authors expanded it with scale-decomposed errors and increment maps.
steps.quote: The purpose of the comparison is to show how similar Local DA analysis with observation-space localization is to the LETKF.

steps.action: Referee 1 asked whether a tighter localization would reduce the noisy analysis; the authors agreed in the rebuttal without a dedicated new test.
steps.quote: Yes, a tight localization length can improve the noisy analysis.

steps.action: Requests from Referees 1 and 2 led to added memory scaling with the number of bands, a clarified localization description, a dimensions table, an operation-count analysis (a theoretical analytical-solution cost was declined), and the stochastic ensemble-update description.
steps.quote: Memory usage increases linearly as the number of wavebands increases.

steps.action: Referee 2 asked to shift the focus to cycling DA; the authors added cycling experiments with ensemble updates (6 h and 3 h intervals) and removed the single-analysis forecasts.
steps.quote: In this revision, we update the ensemble members and examine the DA configurations of Ens_noFLTR and Hybrid_5band_DSL in the cycling DA.

steps.action: Referee 2 questioned using DTE to validate analysis error; the authors kept it, citing Wang et al. (2012).
steps.quote: DTE has been applied to validate the DA analysis and forecast.

steps.action: Referee 2 asked about the spread/RMSE figure; the authors replaced it with new scale-dependent spread-versus-RMSE amplitude and correlation analyses.
steps.quote: This figure has been removed.

steps.action: Referee 2 asked for verification in the typhoon region (10 dBZ or more); the authors computed it, showed it in the rebuttal only, and mention it as not shown.
steps.quote: Usually, the RMSE in this region is larger than that for the whole domain.

steps.action: Referee 2 asked for an imbalance metric; the authors added the surface-pressure tendency analysis and its figure.
steps.quote: We add the related text and a figure (Figure 17) in section 4.3.1.

steps.action: Referee 2 suggested the Fractions Skill Score for reflectivity forecasts; the authors declined because the forecasts were removed.
steps.quote: there is no need to discuss the FSS of reflectivity forecast either.

tree.answer: No natural phenomenon; the object is the performance of a new DA method
Analysis error is measured directly against a known truth in a perfect-model OSSE
Characterize Local DA: analysis quality, continuity, cycling behaviour, cost
Rival configurations: ensemble, static or hybrid covariance; fixed or multiscale localization; model, observation or double space; LETKF
Only loose prior expectations (hybrid helps small ensembles; multiscale beats fixed); no formal distinct predictions
Conditions set in a simulated observing system and nature run
Partly: band numbers, localization space, cycling interval and (not shown) ensemble size varied; one typhoon case only
Kept: hybrid, multiscale and double-space Local DA reduces analysis error; efficiency acceptable
Survived major revision after experiments were redesigned and cycling DA was added

end.claim: Local DA, combining hybrid covariance, model-space multiscale localization and double-space localization, gives lower analysis errors than ensemble-only fixed localization in a simulated typhoon OSSE, without severe discontinuity from local CG solves, and with acceptable parallel efficiency at high memory cost.

decisive_move.sentence: Building the explicit local background-error correlation matrix on observed grid points/columns makes static-correlation hybrids, per-scale localization, double-space localization and the CG solve possible; every claimed result depends on it.

gates.evidence: The experiment set was designed to test expectations from the literature (hybrid helps small ensembles, multiscale beats fixed localization; §1 ¶3, §3.3.1 ¶2), but the simulated data were generated for the method rather than collected under a hypothesis. The claims were scored against a known truth and could have failed; double-space localization alone did not ensure small errors (§4.2 ¶3), and qv errors rose with more bands (§4.2.2 ¶1). Nothing was fixed in advance: localization radii were tuned for the case (§3.3.2 ¶1), and the experiments were redesigned after review (AC1-S p.7–8).

imports.item: Conjugate gradient method (Shewchuk 1994) for solving the local cost function
OpenMP shared-memory parallelization and its scaling limits (Hoeflinger et al. 2001)
Kalman filter framework underlying the LETKF and the stochastic perturbed-observation update

novelty_claims.quote: [...] first paper to report on Local DA
Note that the LETKF of Wang et al. (2021) can also realize double-space localization, but this application has not yet been [...] .
it would be interesting to note the performance of the double-space localization approach, which has not yet been investigated
As the first study to present Local DA, this paper focuses on its idea and basic formulation.

limits: Evidence rests on one simulated typhoon case in a perfect-model OSSE with one analysis time and a short cycling window; no statistical significance is reported for the RMSE differences. Several checks are reported as 'not shown': matrix rank, the observation-operator 2 dBZ gain, N-column degradation, the nature run against CMA, the 36-member ensemble, convective-area errors, and the thinning test. Many parameters are tuned for the case and untested (§3.3.2 ¶1; §5 ¶2), and cross-scale covariance is ignored. Sub-claims and their statuses: no severe CG discontinuity, capability_characterized; affordable Coo with thinning, capability_characterized; similarity to the LETKF under observation-space localization, capability_characterized; hybrid and multiscale benefit in cycling, best_explanation within one case and conditional on a 6 h interval; parallel efficiency, capability_characterized up to 16 cores only. The cause of near-identical Static_BE and Hybrid_noFLTR errors is left unexplained (§4.2.1 ¶2). The review record shows the experiments were redesigned and renamed, and some (LDA_DS_noENS, the 36-member runs, single-analysis forecasts) were removed after review. Inference: the leftover name LDA_HBC_MSL in §4.4 ¶1 suggests the parallel test comes from the pre-review experiment set. The discussion record notes a corrigendum, which was not examined. Composition is none_fits: this is a method-development paper benchmarked by configuration ablations in an OSSE against known truth. It is closest to capability_first, but no phenomenon is established and no explanatory rival is excluded.

disagreements.target: Lei et al. (2021) EnKF-based hybrid using a large (800-member) static ensemble
disagreements.support: The authors argue such large ensembles are often unaffordable and that an LETKF-style hybrid needs them, which motivates computing static correlation explicitly instead.
disagreements.quote: The large ensemble ( > = 800 ) is not always available in practice because of the limited computational and storage resources.

disagreements.target: Common EnKF practice of approximating H from the departure of observation priors from their ensemble mean
disagreements.support: Following Tang et al. (2014) and Yang et al. (2015), the authors use the ensemble mean of model variables instead and report a 2 dBZ reflectivity gain in an unshown early test.
disagreements.quote: Compared with the results using the ensemble mean of observation priors, Eq. (10) reduces the analysis error of reflectivity by approximately 2 dBZ

disagreements.target: Existing spectral-space cross-scale localization (Huang et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2021)
disagreements.support: The authors state these schemes cannot be applied directly in the Local DA correlation formulation; no test is offered.
disagreements.quote: The existing cross-scale localization (e.g., Huang et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2021) is implemented in spectral space and cannot be directly applied

disagreements.target: Concern that double-space localization causes a double penalty
disagreements.support: Double-space localization helped when combined with hybrid and multiscale localization under a noisy ensemble, but the authors restrict its use to such cases and to 3-D DA.
disagreements.quote: [...] , the background error covariance is noisy, so double-space localization has a positive impact.

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Matrix decomposition / eigenvalue decomposition as in the LETKF
alternatives_considered.reason: Decomposition is time-consuming or infeasible for a large Coo (K by K rather than M by M)

alternatives_considered.chosen: Observation prior from the ensemble mean of model variables (Tang et al., 2014)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Ensemble mean of observation priors (standard EnKF approximation)
alternatives_considered.reason: Better results in prior studies, and remote-sensing data matter in a multiscale network

alternatives_considered.chosen: Error correlation matrix as control-variable transform
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Square root of the background error covariance, as in variational DA
alternatives_considered.reason: Square root of a large Coo is expensive; irregular observations preclude a recursive filter
The study mainly concerns the deterministic analysis; ensemble improvement is left to future work

alternatives_considered.chosen: Bandpass as the difference of two Gaussian low-pass analyses (Maddox, 1980)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Many other ways to realize the bandpass filter (unnamed)

alternatives_considered.reason: Cost reduced to about 1/N with acceptable degradation if N < 9

alternatives_considered.chosen: Static part zeroed for cross-variable correlations
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Modeled static cross-variable correlations (e.g., wind-geopotential balance)
alternatives_considered.reason: Static cross-variable correlation must be carefully modeled; work in progress
To avoid issues associated with observation quality control
Hybrid analysis targets small or poor ensembles; computational resources

alternatives_considered.alternatives: No decomposition, two bands, three bands
alternatives_considered.reason: To examine sensitivity to the multiscale configuration

alternatives_considered.chosen: Double-space localization (M+O) for the headline configuration
alternatives_considered.reason: To discuss the impact of localization space
Spin-up needs a sufficiently long interval; the 3 h run shows the imbalance impact
Without thinning the run is very time-consuming and errors rise from correlated observation errors
OpenMP is sufficient for this study; MPI-OpenMP is in progress for larger matrices
